text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The Taleban Islamic militia has offered to hold talks with Afghan opposition forces in the north.
- Eleven people were killed and many hurt by lightning and rain in Sindh, Balochistan and Punjab provinces in the past two days.
- The government ordered sealing of all Pakistan Railway workshops, carriage factories, godowns and stores as part of preparatory measures for privatisation.
- The chairman of state-run Pakistan International Airline, Khakan Abbasi, said privatisation of PIA was not on the priority list of the government.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Foreign and domestic debt estimated at $66 billion now exceeds Pakistan's gross domestic product of about $65 billion.
- The government is considering floating zero coupon bonds of three-year bullet maturity at an annual yield of 13 percent.
- The government intends to raise funds by securitising remittances sent by Pakistanis working abroad.
- The state-run Sui Southern Gas Company Ltd may ask foreign experts to bid for technical advice to help the company plug line leakage that costs millions of rupees a year.
- Smugglers have made inroads into the tea market as legal imports during the first four months of calendar 1997 fell by 34.14 percent, the Pakistan Tea Association said.
THE NATION
- The government has approved a project of 468.866 million rupees to strengthen the meteorological radar network.
- Qazi Hussain Ahmed, chief of the right-wing Jamaat-i-Islami party, said Pakistan would have an Islamic revolution within three months.
- Labour unions are making contact with each other to form a grand alliance to resist privatisation of large service sector corporations such as WAPDA, PTCL, Railways and PIA.
THE FRONTIER POST
- The government has banned the recruitment of women by private companies for overseas employment opportunities.
THE NEWS
- The government will set a target of three months for the banks and development financial institutions to recover at least a third of their total outstanding loans of 130 billion rupees.
- The Lahore-Islamabad motorway project due to be commissioned in August will be delayed for six to 10 months.
-- Islamabad newsroom 274757
